title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-12
body:
Context:
- Incident: sudden throughput regression (~30-50% lower tokens/sec) observed in Dedicated cluster US-west-2 on 2024-11-04 morning deploy. Affects multiple model variants (gptx-13b, opt-13b) when continuous batching enabled. Latency SLOs mostly intact for p95 but tail and aggregate throughput degraded.
- Suspected surface: continuous-batching scheduler changes merged in PR #884 (see linked PR), possible kv-cache/soft-eviction interaction, or changed batching window heuristics.
- Affected pool: dedicated-pool-03 (8 x A100 80GB), kernel build r34, runtime commit a1f2c3d.

Quick timeline (local notes):
- 2024-11-03 22:15 UTC: rolling deploy of runtime commit a1f2c3d -> observed no immediate alarms.
- 2024-11-04 02:30 UTC: customer X reports throughput drop.
- 2024-11-04 03:00 UTC: SRE paged, initial rollback to previous runtime reduces errors but throughput still ~15% lower.
- 2024-11-04 04:15 UTC: Re-enable previous autoscale config, run synthetic load tests.

Observed metrics (baseline vs incident):
- Baseline tokens/sec per GPU (steady, avg): 12k tok/s -> Incident: 7.8k tok/s (~35% drop).
- Avg batch size: baseline 18 tokens/req (batched 20/40 requests) -> incident: observed more small batches average 9 requests/batch.
- Queue waiting time increased (median queue time 15ms -> now 48ms).
- KV-cache hit rate decreased from ~82% -> ~61% for long-lived chat sessions.
- Kernel utilization (SM%) dropped from 68% -> 45%.

Commands / probes I ran (notes + outputs):
1) Check queue/batch stats via /metrics endpoint on node-2:
$ curl -s http://node-2:9090/metrics | grep batching
batching_current_window_ms 12
batching_avg_batch_size 9.1
batching_total_batches 234523

Interpretation: average batch size ~9 (matches infra metrics). Need to find why batching window decreased.

2) Compare config between commits (local git diff of scheduler defaults):
$ git diff origin/main~1..origin/main -- runtime/scheduler/config.yaml
- batching.max_window_ms: 50
- batching.min_batch_size: 8
+ batching.max_window_ms: 25  <-- suspicious
+ batching.min_batch_size: 4  <-- allows smaller batches
+ enable_adaptive_window: true

Note: PR #884 introduced adaptive windowing to lower latency for small requests; might shorten window too aggressively in our workload mix.

3) Inspect logs for explicit evictions / kv-cache warnings:
$ kubectl logs inference-runtime-node-2 | tail -n 200 | grep -Ei "kv-cache|evict|cache miss|cold start|batching"
[2024-11-04T02:12:43Z] WARN kv-cache: eviction triggered, current_entries=124578, max_entries=120000
[2024-11-04T02:12:43Z] INFO batching: forced flush due to max_window_ms reached (25ms)
[2024-11-04T02:15:02Z] WARN kv-cache: miss_rate=0.39, bucket=chat-session-XYZ

Interpretation: eviction cascade observed near incident window. Forced flushes from reduced window value likely causing more cold KV lookups, raising cache misses.

4) Synthetic workload test (local reproducer):
- Playbook: replay 2000 concurrent chat requests with long histories (avg 2k tokens), payloads timed to simulate real traffic distribution.
- With runtime commit a1f2c3d (adaptive window enabled):
  Observed: tokens/sec 7.6k, avg batch size 8.7, kv-cache hit 60%.
- With runtime previous commit a1f2c3c (fixed window 50ms):
  Observed: tokens/sec 11.9k, avg batch size 17.9, kv-cache hit 81%.

5) Heap / memory checks on node-2:
$ ssh node-2 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv'
utilization.gpu [%], utilization.memory [%]
45, 70

$ docker stats --no-stream | grep inference-runtime
inference-runtime  1.2GB / 24GB  45%  1.3%  

No obvious GPU OOMs; memory usage stable. KV-cache eviction is logical, not OOM.

Error snippets worth saving:
- "WARN kv-cache: eviction triggered, current_entries=124578, max_entries=120000"
- "INFO batching: forced flush due to max_window_ms reached (25ms)"
- Intermittent "user-level latency spike: p99 > 3s (kv cache miss path)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Adaptive window change (max_window_ms lowered to 25ms, min_batch_size lowered) causes many forced flushes -> smaller batches -> lower GPU throughput. Also more KV cache lookups because prefix merging less effective -> lower hit rate.
2) KV-cache eviction thresholds too low for long-history chat workload (max_entries configured conservatively). Evictions plus smaller batching window amplify misses.
3) Scheduler change introduced corner-case where certain request ordering causes premature flush (race with request grouping) -> pathological small batches for specific session patterns.
4) Unrelated: driver/kernel regression in r34 reducing kernel occupancy - less likely given rollback still showed improvement only partial.

Quick experiments to validate hypotheses (done / to do):
- Done: Rolled back scheduler to previous config (manually set max_window_ms=50 and min_batch_size=8) in configmap on a staging subset -> synthetic test improved to near baseline.
- Done: Increased kv-cache max_entries by 20% on staging -> hit rate improved + tokens/sec up ~10% (still below baseline unless batching window restored).
- To do: run A/B on live small % of traffic with adaptive_window=false to measure customer impact.
- To do: Add detailed batching trace (per-request batch_id + timestamp) to reproduce ordering corner-case.

Short-term mitigation plan (for on-call / SRE):
1) Set batching.max_window_ms back to 50ms and min_batch_size to 8 in Dedicated pools (hotfix configmap). Roll out to pool-03 only first. Monitor throughput and p95.
2) Increase kv-cache max_entries by 25% for chat-heavy pools to avoid eviction cascades while we tune adaptive window.
3) Disable enable_adaptive_window until we can validate heuristics on mixed workloads.

Longer-term actions (owner/next steps):
- PR: add workload-aware adaptive-window policy that uses historical batch size distribution per-route; fall back safely to fixed window when kv-cache miss increases by >10%.
  - Owner: Amit Patel (actioned in INF-3421)
- Add canary job that runs long-history chat replay on each runtime PR to measure batching & kv-cache interactions automatically.
  - Owner: Jordan Klein
- Add metrics: per-route batch_count histogram, kv-cache-hit-by-age, and batching.forced_flush_reasons (to distinguish manual flush vs max_window).

Notes to self / debugging breadcrumbs:
- Repro steps for local: use chat-replayer with --history-length=2000 --qps=100 and run against single-node runtime with both configs.
- Keep a copy of raw /metrics snapshots and batching traces for 2024-11-04 02:00-05:00 (hours around incident) for postmortem.
- Hypothesis 1 looks strongest: adaptive_window defaults are too aggressive for long-history sessions and reduced window collapses batching benefits -> downstream cache effects amplify the regression.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did rollback (completely reverting runtime) improve errors but not fully recover throughput? (Possible partial config persisted or cache state warmed differently). Need to check if configmap update was complete or some nodes kept older in-memory config until restart.
- Is there any interaction between kernel selection heuristic and smaller batch sizes that amplifies inefficiency? (Need kernel-level profiling for small-batch cases).

References / useful commands saved:
- To restart runtime with new config: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/inference-runtime --namespace=dedicated-pool-03
- To dump batching traces: curl -s http://node-2:9090/debug/batching/trace > batching-trace-node-2-20241104.log
- Synthetic replay tool: tools/chat-replayer --server http://node-2:8080 --concurrency 200 --history-length 2000 --duration 10m

End notes: prioritize immediate config rollback for adaptive_window + increase kv-cache capacity. Follow up with longer-term PR for workload-aware adaptive window and canary tests. Save this scratchpad into Drive before I lose the command history.
